helloSource:
# Hello, TinyCPU: prints a greeting through the CONSOLE register, then reports PASS.
# CONSOLE is at 0x0002_0000 (a store prints its low byte); TOHOST at 0x0002_0004 (1 = PASS).

        .text
_start:
        la      a0, msg         # a0 = address of the string
        call    print_str
        li      t0, 1
        lui     t1, 0x20        # t1 = 0x0002_0000
        sw      t0, 4(t1)       # TOHOST = 1: halt, PASS
halt:   j       halt

# print_str: a0 = address of a NUL-terminated string.
print_str:
        lui     t1, 0x20        # CONSOLE
1:      lbu     t0, 0(a0)
        beqz    t0, 2f
        sb      t0, 0(t1)
        addi    a0, a0, 1
        j       1b
2:      ret

        .data
msg:    .asciz  "Hello, TinyCPU!\n"

fib.source:
# Bubble sort of 12 words in data memory, then print them separated by spaces.

        .text
_start:
        lui     sp, 0x11
        la      s0, array       # s0 = base of the array
        li      s1, 12          # s1 = element count
        addi    s2, s1, -1      # s2 = passes left
1:      blez    s2, 5f
        li      t0, 0           # i
        mv      t1, s0          # t1 = &array[i]
2:      bge     t0, s2, 4f
        lw      a1, 0(t1)
        lw      a2, 4(t1)
        ble     a1, a2, 3f      # already in order
        sw      a2, 0(t1)
        sw      a1, 4(t1)
3:      addi    t0, t0, 1
        addi    t1, t1, 4
        j       2b
4:      addi    s2, s2, -1
        j       1b
5:      li      s2, 0           # print loop
6:      bge     s2, s1, 8f
        slli    t0, s2, 2
        add     t0, t0, s0
        lw      a0, 0(t0)
        call    print_uint
        li      a0, 32          # space
        call    putc
        addi    s2, s2, 1
        j       6b
8:      li      a0, 10          # newline
        call    putc
        j       finish

# print_uint: a0 = unsigned value, printed in decimal (no newline).
print_uint:
        addi    sp, sp, -16
        sw      ra, 12(sp)
        li      t3, 0
        li      t4, 10
1:      mv      t0, a0
        li      t1, 0
2:      bltu    t0, t4, 3f
        addi    t0, t0, -10
        addi    t1, t1, 1
        j       2b
3:      addi    t0, t0, 48
        add     t2, sp, t3
        sb      t0, 0(t2)
        addi    t3, t3, 1
        mv      a0, t1
        bnez    a0, 1b
4:      addi    t3, t3, -1
        add     t2, sp, t3
        lbu     a0, 0(t2)
        call    putc
        bnez    t3, 4b
        lw      ra, 12(sp)
        addi    sp, sp, 16
        ret

# putc: a0 = byte to print.
putc:   lui     t1, 0x20
        sb      a0, 0(t1)
        ret

# finish: report PASS to the harness and halt.
finish: li      t0, 1
        lui     t1, 0x20
        sw      t0, 4(t1)
halt:   j       halt

        .data
        .align  2
array:  .word   42, 7, 99, 3, 18, 64, 1, 27, 85, 11, 50, 5

hazard.title: No dependency
hazard.why: Two instructions that do not touch each other's registers.
hazard.expect: Full throughput: no stalls, and the same cycles with and without forwarding.
hazard.source:
addi t0, zero, 5
addi t1, zero, 6
nop
nop
add t2, t0, t1
ecall

hazard.title: ALU to ALU, distance 1
hazard.why: The next instruction reads a register written by the one just before it.
hazard.expect: Forwarding removes the stall: the forwarded run needs fewer cycles.
hazard.source:
addi t0, zero, 5
addi t1, t0, 1
ecall

hazard.title: ALU to ALU, distance 2
hazard.why: One instruction sits between the producer and the consumer.
hazard.expect: Smaller penalty than distance 1 without forwarding; none with it.
hazard.source:
addi t0, zero, 5
nop
addi t1, t0, 1
ecall

hazard.title: Load-use
hazard.why: A load's value exists only after the MEM stage, so the next instruction must wait one cycle even with forwarding.
hazard.expect: One load-use stall with forwarding on; the stalled run is the slower one.
hazard.source:
lui t0, 0x10          # t0 = 0x0001_0000 (data memory)
lw t1, 0(t0)
addi t2, t1, 1
ecall

hazard.title: Store of a loaded value
hazard.why: The stored register is only needed in EX, so the store can take the value forwarded from WB.
hazard.expect: The load-use stall still happens; the store itself adds none.
hazard.source:
lui t0, 0x10          # t0 = 0x0001_0000 (data memory)
lw t1, 0(t0)
sw t1, 4(t0)
ecall

hazard.title: Store then load of the same word
hazard.why: A load that reads the word a store just wrote: the data memory must return the new value.
hazard.expect: No stall in this design: data memory is write-first, so the load sees the store.
hazard.source:
lui t0, 0x10          # t0 = 0x0001_0000 (data memory)
addi t1, zero, 7
sw t1, 8(t0)
lw t2, 8(t0)
addi t3, t2, 1
ecall

hazard.title: Taken branch
hazard.why: Branches resolve in EX and are predicted not-taken, so a taken one flushes the two instructions behind it.
hazard.expect: Two extra cycles on the pipeline, with or without forwarding; the single-cycle core has none.
hazard.source:
beq zero, zero, skip
addi t0, zero, 1
addi t0, zero, 2
skip: addi t1, zero, 3
ecall

hazard.title: Not-taken branch
hazard.why: The prediction is right, so the instructions behind it keep flowing.
hazard.expect: No flush and no extra cycles.
hazard.source:
bne zero, zero, skip
addi t0, zero, 1
skip: addi t1, zero, 3
ecall
